subject: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finex.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps

Alex / Samir -

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to make the technical feasibility call productive:

Pain points you shared:
- Rising per-token costs on OpenAI/Anthropic, especially for high-volume chat flows and embeddings.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: difficulty porting prompts and tool-calling logic between APIs.
- Occasional latency spikes during peak batch loads impacting user-facing features.
- Security/data residency constraints for EU payments data and some PII.

Current stack (from the call):
- Customer-facing chat/agent flows: OpenAI Chat API (gpt-4 / text-davinci variants) for generative; Anthropic Claude used for a subset of assistant features.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings for search and semantic similarity.
- Orchestration: in-house router that switches models per route; engineering team is comfortable with REST-based SDKs and streaming.

Compatibility & success criteria you mentioned:
- API parity for: streaming responses, function/tool calling (structured tool calls), and reliable embeddings.
- Quality threshold: answers must meet or exceed current subjective quality on our internal eval prompts (we'll share a small prompt set).
- Latency: median per-turn latency within ~20% of current OpenAI baseline; p95 targets aligned with your SLA.
- Cost: target is ~3x reduction in per-token cost for steady-state traffic (rough target for ROI).
- Security: SOC2-compliant controls, VPC/private deployment option for EU data, and KMS integration for keys.

Preliminary open-model shortlist (for discussion on the feasibility call):
- Llama 2 (13B chat) - strong chat baseline, good open community support.
- Mistral Instruct (7B) - efficient option for many instruct tasks with good cost/quality.
- Falcon 40B Instruct - higher capability for harder prompts where LLM reasoning matters.
- RedPajama-INCITE variants - for large-scale embedding and generative experiments.
- Embeddings: consider open embedding models (e.g., SBERT / open embedding families) or Redwood-verified embedding variants.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical feasibility call (30-45m) next week to discuss: prompt examples, exact function-calling needs, streaming expectations, and a small sample dataset for evals.
2) We'll run a short POC: 1 week of bench tests + 3-5 day canary on a small route (we'll propose canary metrics).
3) Procurement checklist + SOC2 and deployment options: attaching a SOC2 summary and our migration playbook for your security team.
4) Quote + rollout plan after POC.

Can you confirm availability for a technical call on Wednesday or Thursday next week (Feb 11-12) in the 9-11am PT window? Also, if you can share the small prompt set and a sample of anonymized inputs (or a redacted dataset) that will help us size the tests.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, migration-playbook-v1.pdf

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0187
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finex.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps

Marissa -

Thanks for the clear recap, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:
- We definitely want streaming and function/tool calling (we have a lambda-based toolchain that expects JSON tool outputs).
- For embeddings: latency is less sensitive but quality for semantic search is critical - we'll share our evaluation prompts.
- Data residency: EU payments data must stay within eu-west-1 and be encrypted at rest with our KMS.

We can do a technical call on Thursday Feb 12 at 10:00am PT. Samir (cc'd) will be the procurement lead on the call and will want a rough timeline and procurement steps (SOW, PO process).

I'll send over a small set of ~20 prompt examples and a redacted sample payload by EOD tomorrow. Please include any SBOM / third-party model licensing notes you think are relevant.

Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Finex Inc
alex.rivera@finex.com | +1 (206) 555-0142
